Forecut India · Summer 27

Air, craft and ease

Near-term forecast · medium directional confidence; product demand unmeasured

Build around breathable separates, fluid drapes and light craft. Reserve sheer, playful and experimental surfaces for small capsules rather than making them the whole range.

Research reviewed 15 October 2026 · Original Forecut analysis

Complete season report with images, all 104 active details, palette, design guidance, calendar and sources.

Direction 01

Cloth before decoration

Summer comfort is the starting point. Develop tactile cotton, linen and fine woven sets whose value comes from handle, proportion and finish.

Build the range
Straight kurta with relaxed trousers; linen overshirt; handloom shirt dress; lightweight everyday saree.
Development notes
Compare unlined and half-lined samples. Test shrinkage, opacity, seam slippage and hand feel after laundering. Avoid heavy fusible panels that defeat airflow.
Commercial action
Protect easy-care core styles; introduce higher-cost handloom in a tightly edited premium capsule. Validate supplier lead times before range sign-off.
Evidence behind this direction
  • Première Vision · SS27 fabric decoding2026-02-13

    Public trade coverage supports light natural blends, fluid shirting, textured weaves and sheer layers. Supplier availability must be verified.

  • ANOKHI · Summer 2026, KambayaSummer 2026 collection

    Indian brand reference for mud-resist, indigo and restrained handmade detailing. A prior-season retail offer, not a 2027 collection.

Direction 02

Light, with coverage

Sheer runway layers become wearable when opacity is designed into the garment. The Indian opportunity is a light overlay with an intentional inner, not an exposed look copied from a show.

Build the range
Organza over cotton-silk; airy cape over a day lehenga; fluid dupatta; sleeveless inner with a loose shirt.
Development notes
Specify inner length, armhole coverage and attachment points. Check snagging, perspiration marks and movement in daylight.
Commercial action
Offer the inner as part of the product; keep the outer usable with existing wardrobe pieces. Test colour and size demand before widening.
Evidence behind this direction
  • Dior · Summer 2027 showSS27 collection

    Sheer and opaque contrasts, light fabrics and floral volume inform occasionwear experimentation. Translate for Indian coverage and climate.

  • Hermès · Women’s spring-summer 2027SS27 collection

    Airy layering and adjustable silk drapes suggest movement-led summer construction; luxury runway evidence does not establish Indian demand.

Direction 03

Playful craft, controlled scale

Use handwork as a recognisable small detail, with clear maker attribution. Current designer and brand references support experimentation without establishing a universal trend.

Build the range
Contrast hand-stitched pockets; crochet-edge shirts; indigo printed co-ords; small patchwork panels.
Development notes
Keep high-labour detailing away from seams and alteration points. Approve print registration, wash fastness and repeatable stitch quality.
Commercial action
Create one recognisable craft code across apparel and a small accessory. Replenish the simpler version if the test performs.
Evidence behind this direction
  • ELLE India · In conversation with Aneeth Arora2026-10-14

    Designer interview offers a journal perspective on péro SS27 and playful craft. Treat as brand intent, not evidence of sales.

  • FDCI · Margn, Circular Design Challenge2026-10-13

    Hand knitting and repurposed materials illustrate small-scale circular design. Commercial consistency and supply still need checking.

  • ANOKHI · Summer 2026, KambayaSummer 2026 collection

    Indian brand reference for mud-resist, indigo and restrained handmade detailing. A prior-season retail offer, not a 2027 collection.

Direction 04

Occasionwear that moves

Bring festive dressing into summer through less bulk and more flexible styling. Practical menswear construction is a relevant Indian lead signal.

Build the range
Light embroidered kurta sets; draped skirt separates; a soft Nehru layer; rewearable wedding-guest lehenga.
Development notes
Use lighter linings, practical pockets and secure drape fastenings. Fit seated, walking and with raised arms; check trim abrasion.
Commercial action
Sell separates with two styling options. Keep ornate pieces in depth-limited occasion drops and compare returns against simpler sets.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

  • FDCI · Aisha Rao, Preyasi2026-07-31

    Textile appliqué, lighter occasion silhouettes and practical pockets provide a useful wedding-guest development reference.

Original working palette

Summer 27 colour direction

Use for sampling and range coordination. Validate physical lab dips under your selling light; these digital colours are not textile standards.

Inky blue#314779

Category opportunities

Womenswear

Prioritise light kurta separates, easy sarees and day-function layers. Test a covered sheer capsule; keep fitted statement bodices selective.

Menswear

Develop linen and cotton-silk kurtas, soft jackets and straight trousers. Comfort construction should be visible in the product explanation.

Fusion & western

Use fluid shirts, relaxed sets and craft accents. Build travel versatility through pockets and adjustable styling rather than excess utility trims.

Footwear

Develop padded flats and flexible occasion shoes. Wide-fit grading, rub testing and outsole grip are essential; no demand uplift is assumed.

Textiles & trims

Cotton, linen blends, light handloom and restrained embroidery lead development. Specify composition, weight and care; do not call a fabric sustainable without proof.

Development calendar

  1. October–November 2026Set customer, occasion and price architecture; source fabric and make first silhouettes.
  2. December 2026Approve washed fit samples, colour fastness, opacity and costing; book craft capacity.
  3. January–February 2027Complete pilot production, product photography and size checks; phase deliveries by climate and occasion.
  4. March–July 2027Review actual full-price sales, returns and replenishment weekly; do not confuse social engagement with purchase.

What would change this forecast?

  • Confirm Holi and Eid drop timing separately; lunar dates can shift.
  • Look for repeated lighter construction across Indian SS27 shows, not one standout look.
  • Stop a sheer or handwork option if opacity, care or quality complaints exceed your own benchmark.

Forecut India · Festive 27

Craft with a second life

Forward forecast · medium-low directional confidence; recheck against 2027 Indian shows

Plan festive capsules around lighter embellishment, adaptable separates and rich textile character. Treat sculptural metallic work as an experimental premium edge rather than a volume assumption.

Research reviewed 15 October 2026 · Original Forecut analysis

Complete season report with images, all 118 active details, palette, design guidance, calendar and sources.

Direction 01

Textile becomes the occasion

Use the weave and placement of craft to create festive identity. The 2026 couture inputs support fresh treatments of familiar techniques, not a claim that every heritage craft is accelerating.

Build the range
Tonal brocade jackets; fine Bandhani drapes; textured silk kurta sets; narrow-border sarees.
Development notes
Approve handloom yardage early. Align motif placement across sizes and price embroidery by actual labour hours.
Commercial action
Pair one statement textile with simpler coordinates. Separate cloth-led premium options from entry-price print interpretations.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Arpita Mehta, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Pastel Bandhani on fluid bases and reinterpretations of Patola and Kantha. Supports craft experimentation, not a mass-market adoption claim.

  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

  • Première Vision · AW27–28 season overviewSeptember 2026 edition

    Public textile-fair overview puts material development at the centre. Used as a long-lead input, not as a reproduced proprietary forecast.

Direction 02

Rewear the celebration

Design wedding-guest pieces to be useful after the event. Lighter construction and modular styling are Forecut development recommendations anchored in current Indian occasionwear practice.

Build the range
Lehenga with a wearable separate blouse; detachable cape; reversible waistcoat; light occasion skirt with pockets.
Development notes
Make fastenings accessible, include alteration allowance and test pocket distortion. Photograph both dressed-up and everyday combinations.
Commercial action
Use bundles and separate purchasing to improve outfit flexibility. Test attach rates before multiplying accessory SKUs.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Aisha Rao, Preyasi2026-07-31

    Textile appliqué, lighter occasion silhouettes and practical pockets provide a useful wedding-guest development reference.

  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

Direction 03

Light as ornament

Material reflection can deliver impact with fewer all-over trims. Reflective couture is a premium signal with substantial weight, repair and sourcing risks.

Build the range
Small pearl-effect borders; metallic-cord accents; controlled tissue panels; a statement brooch.
Development notes
Sample skin contact, sharp edges, tarnishing and storage. Offer repair guidance and keep non-washable components removable where possible.
Commercial action
Keep fragile or expensive surfaces made-to-order or in limited capsules. Never equate couture visibility with volume readiness.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Rimzim Dadu, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Mother-of-pearl and metal-cord couture, with an emphasis on aftercare. A premium experimental signal rather than a volume direction.

  • FDCI · Arpita Mehta, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Pastel Bandhani on fluid bases and reinterpretations of Patola and Kantha. Supports craft experimentation, not a mass-market adoption claim.

Direction 04

Menswear, engineered for the event

Combine Indian textile knowledge with movement and personal styling. Regional weather and event format matter more than a single national festive uniform.

Build the range
Soft bandhgalas; tonal embroidered overshirts; secure draped stoles; straight trousers under layered kurtas.
Development notes
Fit across body types and test long seated wear. Consider breathable linings and secure internal fasteners without replicating a designer’s proprietary mechanism.
Commercial action
Merchandise by event and climate. Offer lighter wedding-guest options beside more elaborate groom pieces.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

Category opportunities

Womenswear

Build saree, blouse and occasion-skirt combinations. Balance craft visibility with weight, alteration access and repeat wear.

Menswear

Focus on tonal texture and comfortable layering; reserve velvet for appropriate winter markets and venues.

Fusion & western

Test occasion jackets over familiar separates. Keep dramatic drapes proportionate and fastening instructions clear.

Footwear

Pair embellished juttis with simpler padded alternatives; run flex, adhesion, grip and long-wear trials.

Textiles & trims

Book tissue, silk blends and artisan embroidery early. Confirm material origin, repairability and actual production capacity before scaling.

Development calendar

  1. January–March 2027Revalidate against Indian runway and brand launches; approve regional assortment and supplier capacity.
  2. April–May 2027Finalise craft strike-offs, fit, wearer trials and cost; retain a fallback fabric for long-lead styles.
  3. June–July 2027Deliver early Rakhi and Onam capsules; stage later festival inventory by verified dates.
  4. August–December 2027Reorder proven shapes. Compare full-price sales, return reasons and repeat purchases by region and event.

What would change this forecast?

  • Recheck couture and textile signals in 2027 before bulk orders.
  • Track whether buyers choose lighter sets at equal prices; there is no sell-through dataset behind this forecast.
  • Test one reflective surface first; discontinue unsafe, heavy or unrepairable options.

Forecut India · Summer 28

An adaptable summer wardrobe

Long-range scenario · low confidence; not observed 2028 runway evidence

Explore fewer, more useful pieces: breathable modular sets, repair-friendly construction and identifiable local craft. These are conditional development scenarios to revisit when 2027–28 signals arrive.

Research reviewed 15 October 2026 · Original Forecut analysis

Complete season report with images, all 112 active details, palette, design guidance, calendar and sources.

Direction 01

Adaptable summer sets

Scenario: versatility becomes a stronger reason to buy if shoppers want fewer occasion-specific pieces. Airy and adjustable 2027 runway ideas are an early design input only.

Build the range
Shirt-and-trouser sets; adjustable wrap kurtas; removable sleeve layers; compact travel capsules.
Development notes
Prototype two ways to wear each piece without excess hardware. Fit-test adjustability at both ends of the size range.
Commercial action
Run a small paid pilot before committing capacity. Compare conversion and repeat wear feedback with fixed styles.
Evidence behind this direction
  • Hermès · Women’s spring-summer 2027SS27 collection

    Airy layering and adjustable silk drapes suggest movement-led summer construction; luxury runway evidence does not establish Indian demand.

  • Première Vision · SS27 fabric decoding2026-02-13

    Public trade coverage supports light natural blends, fluid shirting, textured weaves and sheer layers. Supplier availability must be verified.

Direction 02

Repair is part of the product

Scenario: dependable aftercare helps distinguish premium craft. It depends on service economics and customer adoption, neither of which is established for 2028.

Build the range
Replaceable buttons and ties; spare trim kits; accessible seams; detachable occasion panels.
Development notes
Document repair steps and stock compatible components. Test that removable trims still survive normal wear.
Commercial action
Cost the service separately before promising it. Measure repair use, lead time and margin impact in a pilot.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Rimzim Dadu, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Mother-of-pearl and metal-cord couture, with an emphasis on aftercare. A premium experimental signal rather than a volume direction.

  • Textile Exchange · Materials Benchmark Insights and Trends 20262026 report

    Materials benchmarking highlights the need to distinguish sourcing commitments from actual scale. Circular-material claims require traceable supplier evidence.

Direction 03

Craft with a clear origin

Scenario: customers reward specific provenance over broad craft language. Local making is an identity cue, not automatic proof of lower impact.

Build the range
Cluster-attributed handloom shirts; small-batch indigo sets; restrained crochet and embroidery accents.
Development notes
Record fibre composition, supplier and process; check batch consistency and substantiate any environmental claim.
Commercial action
Test product descriptions that explain maker and technique. Validate willingness to pay rather than assuming a premium.
Evidence behind this direction
  • ANOKHI · Summer 2026, KambayaSummer 2026 collection

    Indian brand reference for mud-resist, indigo and restrained handmade detailing. A prior-season retail offer, not a 2027 collection.

  • FDCI · Margn, Circular Design Challenge2026-10-13

    Hand knitting and repurposed materials illustrate small-scale circular design. Commercial consistency and supply still need checking.

  • Textile Exchange · Materials Benchmark Insights and Trends 20262026 report

    Materials benchmarking highlights the need to distinguish sourcing commitments from actual scale. Circular-material claims require traceable supplier evidence.

Direction 04

Soft structure for daily dressing

Scenario: summer tailoring stays relaxed while becoming more purposeful. Build recognisable shapes with better finishing instead of adding novelty to every style.

Build the range
Unstructured overshirts; fluid sarees; straight-leg trousers; breathable waistcoats.
Development notes
Check drape, collar recovery, seam stability and opacity. Build wear trials into development before range expansion.
Commercial action
Retain a familiar core and trial one silhouette change at a time. Use actual return reasons to set revisions.
Evidence behind this direction
  • Première Vision · SS27 fabric decoding2026-02-13

    Public trade coverage supports light natural blends, fluid shirting, textured weaves and sheer layers. Supplier availability must be verified.

  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

Forecut India · Festive 28

Celebration, built to keep

Long-range scenario · low confidence; review before any commercial commitment

Explore occasionwear whose value comes from reconfiguration, provenance and aftercare. This is an original Forecut planning scenario, not a claim about confirmed 2028 consumer preferences or designer collections.

Research reviewed 15 October 2026 · Original Forecut analysis

Complete season report with images, all 113 active details, palette, design guidance, calendar and sources.

Direction 01

The occasion wardrobe, recomposed

Scenario: an existing saree, skirt or kurta gains new life through a fresh layer. Current modular and lighter-occasion inputs support prototyping, not a prediction of guaranteed uptake.

Build the range
Detachable draped panels; separate capes; reversible occasion jackets; mixable saree blouses.
Development notes
Make attachment points discreet and stress-test them. Check fit when parts are used independently.
Commercial action
Pilot a wardrobe-refresh capsule beside complete looks. Compare attachment sales with unsold component stock.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Aisha Rao, Preyasi2026-07-31

    Textile appliqué, lighter occasion silhouettes and practical pockets provide a useful wedding-guest development reference.

  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

Direction 02

Heirloom surfaces, modern placement

Scenario: restrained craft placement makes premium pieces easier to wear again. Heritage should be credited rather than reduced to a generic luxury claim.

Build the range
Narrow woven borders; tonal Bandhani; placed Kantha-inspired handwork through the appropriate maker partnership.
Development notes
Approve stitch density and motif placement on actual size sets. Build traceability and artisan payment into sourcing briefs.
Commercial action
Test one craft family across a limited range. Validate lead times and gross margin after handwork and finishing costs.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Arpita Mehta, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Pastel Bandhani on fluid bases and reinterpretations of Patola and Kantha. Supports craft experimentation, not a mass-market adoption claim.

  • Première Vision · AW27–28 season overviewSeptember 2026 edition

    Public textile-fair overview puts material development at the centre. Used as a long-lead input, not as a reproduced proprietary forecast.

Direction 03

Repairable occasion shine

Scenario: aftercare becomes part of the premium proposition. Reflective couture offers a visual reference but creates particular durability and storage challenges.

Build the range
Replaceable decorative panels; removable brooches; controlled metallic accents; spare embellished patches.
Development notes
Test abrasion, humidity exposure, trim replacement and packing. Supply a realistic care card and repair route.
Commercial action
Keep experimental materials in made-to-order or limited runs. Expand only after repair and defect costs are understood.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Rimzim Dadu, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Mother-of-pearl and metal-cord couture, with an emphasis on aftercare. A premium experimental signal rather than a volume direction.

  • Textile Exchange · Materials Benchmark Insights and Trends 20262026 report

    Materials benchmarking highlights the need to distinguish sourcing commitments from actual scale. Circular-material claims require traceable supplier evidence.

Direction 04

Local making, contemporary shape

Scenario: recognisable local techniques pair with contemporary separates. The opportunity depends on supply reliability and demonstrated customer interest.

Build the range
Light craft jackets; textured straight kurtas; draped skirts with pockets; simple occasion footwear.
Development notes
Obtain material and process records. Fit-test for movement and avoid unsupported recycled, regenerative or biodegradable claims.
Commercial action
Use pre-orders or small pilots to learn about demand. Revisit the range after 2027 and 2028 Indian shows.
Evidence behind this direction
  • FDCI · Margn, Circular Design Challenge2026-10-13

    Hand knitting and repurposed materials illustrate small-scale circular design. Commercial consistency and supply still need checking.

  • FDCI · Kunal Rawal, India Couture Week 20262026-07-28

    Designer interview: functional linings, wearable drapes and tonal craft in menswear. An occasionwear input, not measured retail demand.

  • Textile Exchange · Materials Benchmark Insights and Trends 20262026 report

    Materials benchmarking highlights the need to distinguish sourcing commitments from actual scale. Circular-material claims require traceable supplier evidence.

Category opportunities

Womenswear

Explore reconfigurable saree and skirt outfits and placed craft. Avoid extending today’s trend curve automatically into 2028.

Menswear

Explore contemporary jackets, draped accessories and comfortable occasion trousers; test regional temperature needs.

Fusion & western

Explore component-led occasion capsules that work with existing wardrobe basics. Validate mix-and-match fit and styling clarity.

Footwear

Explore repair-friendly occasion flats and removable decorative elements where safe; wear and snag testing come first.

Textiles & trims

Prioritise verifiable origin and repeatable quality. Keep novel material development conditional on testing and commercial supply.

Development calendar

  1. July–December 2027Check Indian couture, festive retail and trade-fair developments; replace unsupported scenarios.
  2. January–March 2028Validate target customers, price tolerance and suppliers; approve initial prototypes.
  3. April–July 2028Run wear, repair and quality tests; lock only proven options and verified festival delivery windows.
  4. August–December 2028Monitor sell-through and returns by event and region; record which hypotheses actually performed.

What would change this forecast?

  • Do not use 2026 couture as proof of 2028 mass-market adoption.
  • Stop material experiments when safe care or repair cannot be offered.
  • Replace this scenario with direct 2028 evidence as it becomes available; next planned research checkpoint: July 2027.
